title.title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over every global field
title.subtitle: Claim: normal subgroups of $G(k)$ come only from the places where $G$ is anisotropic

beats.text: Normal subgroups of $G(k)$ should come only from places where $G$ is compact
Isotropic groups and inner type $A$ were known (grey)
Claimed (dashed): the last anisotropic types and all function fields, char 2 included

sources.quote: Remaining open: anisotropic outer forms of type A, trialitarian D4 and certain E6
For every global field k (number fields and function fields, including characteristic 2)
there is an open normal W in H_A with N = delta_A^{-1}(W)
it uses the classification of finite simple groups in places
read each family's summary and abstracts and the introduction and main theorem of every principal paper

plain: In arithmetic symmetry groups, every normal subgroup comes from the obvious source: no surprise ones

steps: Suppose a surprise normal subgroup existed
Dividing by it would leave a finite quotient group
For these last group types such quotients can't exist

voice.text: Normal subgroups should come only from compact places. A few exceptional types stayed open.
A surprise subgroup would leave a finite quotient, which cannot exist here.
Claimed: every global field, characteristic two included.
